items.q: Severe ear pain worsened by pressing the tragus, with a swollen canal and normal drum, indicates what?
items.exp: Canal inflammation hurts on tragus pressure and pinna traction, and the drum stays normal behind oedematous canal. Middle ear disease instead bulges the drum without tragus tenderness.
r: Incorrect. Middle ear pain spares tragus pressure and bulges the drum.
Correct. Tragus tenderness plus canal swelling means otitis externa.
Incorrect. Otosclerosis deafens painlessly with normal canal.
Incorrect. Meniere causes vertigo and aural fullness, not canal pain.
items.kp: Pain on tragus press: think canal, not middle ear.

items.q: Elderly diabetic with deep nocturnal ear pain and granulations at the canal floor most likely has what?
items.exp: Necrotising otitis externa is pseudomonal skull base osteomyelitis of elderly diabetics: night pain, junction granulations, cranial nerve risk. It needs systemic antipseudomonal therapy.
r: Incorrect. Furuncle is a localised outer canal staphylococcal boil.
Correct. Diabetic night pain with granulations means malignant otitis externa.
Incorrect. Wax blocks quietly without granulations.
Incorrect. Eczema itches and scales without bone invasion.
items.kp: Old diabetic, night pain, granulations: skull base infection until disproven.

items.q: Wax removal by syringing is contraindicated when which condition exists?
items.exp: Syringing a perforated ear drives infected water into the middle ear and mastoid. Use microsuction under vision instead when the drum is perforated or surgery history exists.
r: Incorrect. Hard symptomatic wax is itself an indication with intact drum.
Correct. Perforation forbids blind syringing.
Incorrect. Both ears may be cleared safely if drums intact.
Incorrect. Itch alone needs diagnosis before any clearing.
items.kp: No drum, no syringe: clear under vision.

items.q: Blisters on the concha with ipsilateral facial palsy define which syndrome?
items.exp: Varicella zoster reactivation in the geniculate ganglion causes Ramsay Hunt: conchal vesicles, facial palsy and ear pain, often with vertigo. Early antivirals and steroids help recovery.
r: Incorrect. Bell palsy lacks vesicles and ear lesions.
Correct. Vesicles plus facial palsy mean Ramsay Hunt.
Incorrect. Gradenigo adds abducens palsy and retro-orbital pain from petrositis.
Incorrect. Frey is gustatory sweating after parotid surgery.
items.kp: Ear blisters plus weak face equals shingles of the facial nerve.

items.q: A boxer with a tense fluctuant pinna swelling after a blow needs what urgently?
items.exp: Auricular haematoma separates perichondrium from cartilage; undrained blood necroses cartilage into cauliflower ear. Aspiration or incision plus compression prevents deformity.
r: Incorrect. Untreated haematoma permanently deforms the ear.
Correct. Drain and compress to save cartilage.
Incorrect. Steroids do not remove the blood collection.
Incorrect. Canal cleaning is irrelevant to pinna haematoma.
items.kp: Drain it and press it, or the ear crumples.

items.q: Fungal otitis externa (otomycosis) is most often precipitated by what?
items.exp: Long topical antibiotics suppress bacteria and let Aspergillus and Candida flourish, giving itchy canal debris with visible fungal elements. Thorough toilet and antifungal therapy cure it.
r: Incorrect. Water favours bacterial Pseudomonas disease mainly.
Correct. Prolonged antibiotic drops breed otomycosis.
Incorrect. Clearing wax under vision does not cause fungal disease.
Incorrect. Hearing aids may macerate but drops are classic precipitant.
items.kp: Itchy ear after weeks of drops: look for fungus.

items.q: Perichondritis of the pinna characteristically spares which part?
items.exp: The lobule contains no cartilage, so cartilage infection (perichondritis) spares it while bacterial cellulitis involves it. Pseudomonas after piercing is typical and cartilage needs prompt systemic cover.
r: Incorrect. Helix is cartilage and inflames.
Correct. No cartilage in lobule, so perichondritis spares it.
Incorrect. Antihelix cartilage is involved.
Incorrect. Tragus cartilage can be involved.
items.kp: Sore pinna sparing lobule equals cartilage disease.

items.q: Bony canal swellings in a cold water swimmer narrowing both canals are most likely what?
items.exp: Cold water induces multiple bilateral bony exostoses narrowing canals, trapping wax and water. Solitary unilateral pedunculated bony mass is osteoma instead. Surgery only when symptomatic.
r: Incorrect. Osteoma is usually solitary and unilateral.
Correct. Multiple bilateral bony humps in swimmers are exostoses.
Incorrect. Cholesteatoma gives keratin debris and erosion, not native bone humps.
Incorrect. Foreign bodies are objects, not fixed bony walls.
items.kp: Cold water plus bilateral bony narrowing means surfer ear.

items.q: Canal furuncle causes pain mainly located where and from what infection?
o: Outer cartilaginous canal hair follicle; staphylococcal
items.exp: Hair follicles exist only in outer cartilaginous canal, so staphylococcal furuncles sit there and hurt on jaw movement. Inner bony canal has no follicles. Most settle with analgesia and local care.
r: Incorrect. Inner canal lacks hair follicles and viral boils.
Correct. Outer canal follicle staphylococcal abscess is a furuncle.
Incorrect. That describes otitis media instead.
Incorrect. Mastoid pseudomonas disease is malignant otitis pattern.
items.kp: Boils grow only where hairs grow: outer canal.

items.q: First step for a live insect in the ear canal is what?
o: Immobilise with oil or alcohol then remove under vision
items.exp: Killing or immobilising the insect with oil prevents painful movement and bites, then remove by suction or forceps under vision. Cotton buds push objects deeper and injure drums.
r: Incorrect. Syringing a live insect causes frantic movement and pain.
Correct. Still it with oil, then remove under vision.
Incorrect. Buds push deeper and perforate drums.
Incorrect. Retained insects damage canal and drum.
items.kp: Still the insect first, then lift it out under sight.
